abstract: The clinical, radiologic, cytopathologic and histologic features of a case of spermatocytic seminoma in a 56-year-old man are reported and discussed. The cytologic findings in fine needle aspiration (FNA) smears suggested a diagnosis of spermatocytic seminoma, which was confirmed by subsequent histopathologic studies. The case suggests that spermatocytic seminoma can be suspected and distinguished from other types of seminoma and germ cell neoplasms by FNA cytology. The following criteria appear to be the most useful in making the cytodiagnosis: the presence of three different types of cells (large, medium and small), a clean background, an absence of a lymphoid component and "tigroid" substances and the relative paucity and clumping tendency of the neoplastic cells in the smears.
abstract_ja: 56歳男性の精子細胞性セミノーマの臨床、放射線学、細胞診、組織学的特徴を報告し、考察した。FNA塗抹標本の細胞診所見から精子細胞性セミノーマが疑われ、その後の組織学的検討で確定された。本症例は、FNA細胞診によりセミノーマや他の型の胚細胞腫瘍と区別できることを示唆している。細胞診の診断に有用と考えられた基準は以下のとおりである:3種類の異なる細胞型(大、中、小)の存在、清明な背景、リンパ球成分の欠如、「tigroid」物質、そして腫瘍細胞の比較的少なさと凝集傾向。
